title: A file of the catalog of jef-sure/boards, format version 2 (draft for review)
description: One schema for the generator and the editor. The root checks the shape of a file as written; #/$defs/resolved checks a board after the layers are merged. Fields named x_* are free and tools do not read them.

class.description: One role, or several for a chip that has them. Tools read it as an array.

maker.description: Who makes it: a short name of ours. The name for devicetree is compat.

tariff.description: The customs tariff code of the goods: HS or CN, digits only. Duties on small parcels are counted by it.

price.description: What one unit costs, by offer: named entries, so a layer can add one. Costs of an order, as delivery and duty, are not here: they depend on the whole order.

range.description: Lowest and highest price of one unit. Less than 3 is [0, 3]: a bound, not an invented low, and a kit counts it as 3.

qty.description: The least quantity this price holds for. 1 when absent.

compat.description: The compatible of devicetree, where the chip has one. The only field kept for a format outside.

draw.description: Current by mode, such as active or sleep, in mA. What it stands on goes in checked.

notes.description: What is special about this, in words, for a person: one text, or one entry for each thing. Tools show it and do not read it.

level.description: Where a fact comes from, most trusted first: this order is the scale. hardware: tried on a board. schematic and datasheet: the maker's drawings and the chip's. vendor-docs: the maker's specifications and pin tables. vendor-code: the maker's examples, a hint. community: other people's descriptions. extracted: taken by a tool, read by nobody. unchecked: from memory.

checked.description: What the facts of this file stand on, entry by entry. Named entries, so a layer can add one: the person who tries an imported board adds what was confirmed. Without covers an entry is about the whole file.

covers.description: Paths in this file, as devices.touch or connectors.CN1.

source.description: The document, its version and where it was found.

unit.description: Which board was tried: on_board names a model, this names one piece of it.

result.description: confirmed when absent. refuted keeps a disagreement in sight; pending says what is still to be tried.

on_board.description: Made by the loader: this entry was earned by the board named, a variant only inherits it.

origin.description: Where this file came from when it was imported. It says nothing of how true it is: that is checked.

images.description: Pictures for people; a program and an agent need nothing from them. A connector's at names one of these.

source.description: Whose picture: own, or where the right to use it comes from. Vendor photos are not copied.

up.description: Where the top of the screen points, so as the board shows it needs no words.

line.description: A wire: a GPIO, "nc" when not wired, or an object: a GPIO with its properties, a bit of an expander, a rail of a PMIC, a channel of an ADC. null is not a value: in a layer it removes the field.

analog.description: Read through the ADC: the window of this line in millivolts. Buttons on a resistor ladder share one GPIO, each with its window.

buses.description: Kinds of buses, each with named buses. The name of an SPI, I2C or I2S bus is the host or port of the chip; soft<n> is a bus made in software. A kind not listed is kept as data.

busI2s.description: Standard I2S and TDM have bclk and ws, PDM has clk: "nc" for a PDM output with no clock line, into a filter. The extra data lines are of PDM. Whether a device on it uses std, tdm or pdm is in its connection: the two directions of a port can differ.

lane_mbps.description: Of a panel, measured on a board: a board with a connector and no panel has none.

busCsi.description: MIPI CSI: the lanes have pins of their own, no GPIO. lane_mbps is of a mode of the sensor, when a board holds one.

busDvp.description: The parallel camera port. de is HREF of the sensor; XCLK is a line of the camera, in its pins.

connection.description: One bus of a device: what belongs to this connection, not to the device or the bus.

lines.description: In a type: the lines the chip needs beside this bus, which a board wires in pins.

format.description: Of an I2S bus: how this device uses it. std when absent.

sio.description: Of an SPI bus: data both ways on MOSI, MISO unused.

required.description: In a type: this kind of bus must be wired.

on.description: kind in a type or a module; kind.name or kind.mux.chN on a board.

control.description: A parameter that can differ from what the device starts with. how: what sets it, from a closed list; each way that a program can take is one C function in src/. read: how its value can be known.

values.description: A list, or positions by value for a switch.

lines.description: The switches or jumpers, as the board names them.

start.description: The value of the board at start.

capability.description: What a device gives, with its figures. output: what it can report; specified: where the maker promises accuracy. A limit of the chip belongs here, a limit of a library in its record, a figure of an antenna or a module in the module or the board.

modes.description: How it works: reader, peer_to_peer, card_emulation for NFC.

targets_max.description: How many it handles at once.

width_max.description: Of a sensor: its largest picture.

formats.description: Of a sensor: the pixel formats it gives, as raw10 or rgb565.

freq_mhz.description: The carrier, lowest and highest. One frequency is [13.56, 13.56].

tx_mw_max.description: The most the transmitter takes from its supply. What leaves the antenna is less: radiated_mw.

radiated_mw.description: What leaves the antenna. It depends on the antenna, so a module or a board keeps it, measured, in checked.

range_mm.description: How far it works, with this antenna. A range is a guide from experience; the low end counts against what is asked.

reads.description: Distances measured: by card and through what.

features.description: What the chip does by itself, as lpcd, dpc, awc, crypto1 for NFC.

frame_bytes.description: The largest frame or FIFO of the chip.

stack.description: Who runs ISO 14443-4: the firmware of the chip or the program.

device.description: A device on a board or in a module. With chip, the entry of the catalog lies under it.

part.description: The maker's part number, when the chip's entry does not say it or says less.

marking.description: What the package shows, when the part is not known.

ref.description: Its designator on the schematic, as U6.

count.description: How many of this one product takes, for what has no wiring of its own: screws, cables. 1 when absent.

chip_try.description: A chip found at start: one of these, in the order to try. It stands instead of chip, so the class is the device's own.

logic.description: The step of power a high level on the lines of this device reaches: where its pull-ups go, or what its outputs drive. none: it puts nothing on them, as a display with no line back.

classes.description: Made by the loader: class as an array.

wants.description: Made by the loader: the kinds of bus the type asks for, with the lines each needs.

library.description: Which library of the chip this device uses; the loader fills it in when the catalog has one.

needs.description: What the program needs of the library, by thing, as its supports names them.

libraries.description: Made by the loader: the entries of this chip in the libraries of the catalog.

library_version.description: The version of the library, when it is not the newest the catalog describes.

library_at.description: Made by the loader: the version of the library the checks are about.

firmware_version.description: The firmware of this device, when it is not the newest the catalog describes.

antenna.description: The antenna of a radio or a reader: it is not the chip's, so its figures lie with the module or the board that has it.

defer.description: Starts after the first event, such as a CST816T that is silent until touched.

identify.description: How a program tells this chip from its clones: a register and what it holds in the original.

part.description: The maker's part number; a family says it in each variant.

variants.description: The members of a family: each is a patch over this file.

variant_by.description: What sets the variant and how a program can know it.

high_mv_max.description: The most a pin takes as a high level, at the usual supply of its domain.

pins.description: What each GPIO can do besides being one, by its number. From the documentation of ESP-IDF.

notes.description: What those notes mean, and when a pin may be used.

frequency_sources.description: Where the chip gets a frequency, in the order to try them.

limits.description: The largest speeds of the chip, in MHz.

revisions.description: How the revisions of the silicon differ: this file describes the newest, a step patches the revisions before `before`.

options.description: The minimum revisions the configuration offers, 100 for 1.0.

sdkconfig.description: How a revision and its speeds are set: a symbol for each, with {value}, and lines of its own.

volts.description: One voltage, or the range a device on it must take.

mechanics.description: The board as a thing to fit in a case. Coordinates from its centre, y up.

rates.description: What one unit of the base currency buys in others, on one day: catalog/rates.json, written by tools/update_rates.py.

frequencySource.description: A part of a chip that makes a frequency. A frequency belongs to a timer, so outputs of one setting share it.

kind.description: How the frequency is made: the solver has a formula for each.

pairs.description: It can drive two pins in antiphase.

can.description: What can be changed while it runs.

signals.description: Clocks of the board it can bring to a pin.

selection.description: selection.json of a project: how its kit was chosen, written by the page and read back when the folder is opened.

answers.description: By the id of the question.

says.description: What the kit said, as it was shown.

rejected.description: The boards that did not fit, and why.

way.description: One way to wire a device with no bus: its lines, and what it gives on them. The fewest lines come first.

ledc.description: The LEDC channels one device takes this way.

gives.description: The figures of this way, as swing_v across a piezo disc.

do.description: What a person does to wire it.

pins.description: What each contact carries, from contact 1.

part.description: The chip as its maker names it, as ESP32-D0WD-V3.

controls.description: Values for the parameters of the chip, such as wifi_tx_power.

facts.description: Made by the loader: the entry of catalog/mcu/.

psram_mhz.description: A PSRAM clock below what the revision takes, when the board holds it down; none: the largest it takes.

revision.description: The revision of the chip on this board, as the bootloader prints it; board_select.py --revision takes another.

cpu_mhz.description: A clock below what the revision takes; none: the largest it takes.

powerStep.description: A line of supply or a strobe. The list is the order of the start, so a step takes only from a step before it. A step with a name is a line of supply and owns its GPIO; one with none is a strobe on a line a device owns.

name.description: As the schematic or the board writes it. A contact of a connector with this text is this line.

source.description: Where a supply comes in. connector: a module takes it from the board it is on.

from.description: The step it takes from, or several, each with its own way in.

regulator.description: How the voltage changes: an ldo passes its current on, the others convert power.

line.description: What switches it, or the rail of a PMIC. A line a device owns stays there: why says it.

volts.description: What a step with source connector takes from the board.

feeds.description: What it feeds: devices, mcu, or a step of a module. A chip on two lines is in both.

powerThrough.description: The device it goes through, or several in order: a regulator, a diode, a fuse.

dropout.description: What is lost from input to output: the least an ldo needs, the drop of a diode.

resolved.description: A board or module after the layers are merged and the catalog applied.

window_mm.description: The opening that shows the panel, where the area of its pixels is not measured.

timing.description: Of a panel fed without pause, RGB or MIPI-DSI video. What it stands on goes in checked: a maker's figures are a hint until measured on the board.

pclk_edge.description: The edge the panel takes data on. rising when absent.

refresh.description: How the picture changes: full and partial are e-paper.

band_bytes.description: The size of a piece of a frame that suits this panel.

init.description: The init sequence with its source, for libraries that have no driver for the panel.

over.description: The display the touch lies over, or "none". The calibration is for that display.

x_max.description: The largest raw coordinate, not their number.

fingers.description: It comes from the chip's entry; a board writes it when it differs.

calibrations.description: What was measured on this panel, one entry a measurement, the newest last; the last is taken for now.

questions.description: catalog/questions.json: what the selection asks. The form of the page comes from it.

type.description: outputs: a list of tones and PWM signals, each with its frequency and what it needs.

top.description: Shown in the top row of the page, not among the questions about the hardware.

when.description: It is asked only when these answers are given, by the id of the question. true: any answer but none; {"at_least": n}: a count of n or more.

limit.description: What a number limits instead of asking for a part.

of.description: The class it is measured on.

questionNeed.description: What an answer asks of a board: a device of a class, or what the board provides.

where.description: What the device must have, by the path of the field.

calibration.description: The places aimed at, each named for where it is on the display in its own orientation. The corners are required: TFT_eSPI and LovyanGFX calibrate by them. What only one library uses lies under libraries.

rule.description: When this measurement holds, in words for now: tools do not read it yet.

measured_with.description: The versions it was measured with, by library: a calibration holds for what it was measured on.

x_max.description: The range of the touch it was measured with.

width.description: The size of the display it was measured under, in its own orientation.

libraries.description: What only one library uses, by library.

meant.description: Where it was aimed, in pixels of the display in its own orientation.

device.description: What the touch controller reported there, in its own coordinates.

calibrationDgxDi.description: What dgx_di_calibrate_measure adds to the points. The glue makes the record of DGX-DI from the points at start.

rounds.description: Rounds of targets the measurement took.

blink_ms.description: The longest the panel showed a finger near the glass.

gap_ms.description: The longest it lost a finger held.

off_tenths.description: How far off the touches were without the calibration, on average, in tenths of a pixel.

clock.description: What the codec takes its clock from. mclk when absent.

camera.description: A sensor on a bus for its picture and usually I2C for its registers. chip may be missing: an imported board often does not name the sensor.

xclk_hz.description: The clock the board gives the sensor on pins.xclk.

divider.description: The battery through top_ohm to the ADC, bottom_ohm from there to ground. switch feeds it only for a reading, settle_us after that.

buttons.description: The buttons of the standard set by role; a pad with a chip of its own has none here.

libraryId.description: ecosystem/owner/name, the path of the record under catalog/libraries/.

libraryStep.description: One step of a start: a call, a control applied with its value of the board, or a line set. {name} in args is a value the caller gives.

for.description: Only for this use, such as a protocol.

ok.description: How its result shows it worked, by the conventions of its library: equals, not, or none for a call that gives no result.

libraryTransport.description: How the library sets up a kind of bus.

shared.description: On a bus set up before.

libraryChip.description: What the library does with one chip: how it starts it, what it can do with it.

interface.description: The common interface it is reached through.

setup.description: What follows the init, in order.

adapter.description: This component can start this chip with this library.

headers.description: What the glue includes for this chip.

firmware.description: The firmware of the chip it takes, as a range.

via.description: The ways that have this version, when not all of install do.

frameworks.description: What its code is built against, with the versions: esp-idf, arduino-esp32 and the like. A library for several has several.

targets.description: The chips it builds for, when it limits them. No list says nothing: it may have declared none.

ecosystem.description: Where it is published: the registry its name belongs to, not what it builds with. A new one is a new directory.

license.description: Of the version described, as an SPDX expression where it has one; history says when it was another.

interfaces.description: Common interfaces it takes other drivers through.

groups.description: How it joins displays, by display_groups.how.

values.description: Its names for the values of the data.

adapter.description: How this component takes it: the version its code is written against and the symbols of its rules.

headers.description: What the generated glue includes, private to the adapter.

public.description: The header that gives a program the handles of this library, in include/ of the adapter.

sources.description: What adapters/<owner>__<name>/ compiles, by the Kconfig symbol that brings it.

described.description: The version the record describes: what it says of chips is true of this one.

scheme.description: How the parts of its version numbers compare; the numbers stay as the maker writes them.

libraryHistory.description: How the versions before `before` differed: each field is a Merge Patch over that field of the record; null removes.

firmware.description: Software inside the device that changes what it can do. Patches of older versions lie in history.

kept.description: Where it lives; none: the host writes it at every start.

described.description: The version the file of the device describes.

scheme.description: How the parts of its version numbers compare; the numbers stay as the maker writes them.

libraryInstall.description: One way to get a library. The list goes from the way to prefer.

via.description: platform: it comes with the framework, nothing to download.

path.description: Where it lies inside the repository.

ref.description: The tag of a version, with {version} in it, or a branch. None: the default branch.

assembly.description: What a board and a module share: a module is a board used as a part of another. It may have a chip of its own, like a C6 on the SDIO of a P4.

extends.description: The board this one is a variant of.

part.description: The maker's name for this board or module.

revision.description: The revision of the printed board this file describes, as its maker writes it.

do.description: What a person does to fit it, beside the wires. A kit shows these.

modules.description: Modules on this board. on says which bus each kind of bus of the module joins; pins and config are for a module of one part. A part is named <use>_<part>.

supply.description: The line of the board each step of the module with source connector takes from, by the name of the step.

devices.description: The wiring of each part of the module, by its name there: a layer over that part.

display_groups.description: Displays shown as one screen. side_by_side is dgx_vscreen_2h_init(left, right): the width adds up, the height is the larger.

power.description: Rails and strobes to set before the devices start, in this order.

shared_pins.description: Lines several devices use on purpose.

only_while.description: The line is free for the others only while this parameter has this value: TE of a panel on the pin of a button.

of.description: A directory of catalog/connectors/: a connector whose contacts are fixed by a standard.
